correctness.rationale: For every positive smoothing variance and fixed deterministic mean, the pivot-conditioned integral has weight x²/(x²+S) and a Gaussian pivot density strictly positive at x=0. Triangle inequalities trap the large Schur complement event at |x| of order ||u||||v||/t; weighted integration gives exactly (2/3)f(0)(||u||||v||)^3/S. Uniform domination uses ||u||||v||≤S/2, finite Gaussian complement fourth moments and exponentially light discarded W. Finite sum yields positive noncentral constant; centered chi-square/Dirichlet calculation gives the claimed gamma ratio. Layer-cake proves finite moments exactly below order three. The exact oriented-minor identity and independent Gaussian radial scaling recover the correctly credited mean-square formula. The supplied program passed 175 deterministic identities and millions of non-exhaustive simulations.

value.rationale: For a recent randomized numerical pivoting method, expected-square estimates miss a sharp failure of all third or higher residual moments, robust to arbitrary deterministic data and even arbitrarily small Gaussian perturbation. The exact coefficient supplies nontrivial dimension and noise dependence. This matters for risk-sensitive low-rank approximation and contrasts sharply with maximum-entry pivoting, whose Gaussian-input moments all exist. It is neither a renaming nor a special case of the existing expected-square result.
